derivedFrom: the trend rule and the tranche rules settled at 4.0, applied to the committed bar files and the levels expectation outside this repository and without running the ladder builder. The bars are adjusted first, the factor being the provider's adjusted close over its raw close with the high and low scaled by the same figure. The averages are the arithmetic mean of the last 50 and the last 200 adjusted closes. The swings are sessions whose high is strictly above all six neighbours or whose low is strictly below all six. The tranches are the support bands whose low edge is below the close, nearest first, at most three, skipping any band with no anchor other than a moving average; each stop is the low edge of the next support band beneath it whatever anchors that one in a range, and in an uptrend the higher of that band and the most recent swing low beneath the tranche; the invalidation is the lowest of those stops, or a tranche's own low edge where no band sits beneath it. The typical day's move is twice the merge distance the levels expectation states, the merge distance being half of it. Nothing here was read back from a run.
note: a row is written for every current index member and not only the names carrying a plan, so the row count is the membership expectation's currentMembers and never the count of names with a tranche. The two departed constituents get no row, because they are not members tonight.

inputs.note: what the rule read, stated so a disagreement can be traced to a figure rather than to the answer. Prices are strings because they are prices; the averages are quoted to the four places the store carries.

AAPL.why: close above the 50, the 50 above the 200, and the last swing low above the one before it

KEYS.why: close above the 50 by about a point, the 50 above the 200, and the last swing low above the one before it. The nearest of the four to changing its answer: a close a dollar lower is a range.

MSFT.why: close above the 50, the 50 above the 200, and the last swing low a hundred points above the one before it

NFLX.why: the averages disagree with each other. The close is above the 50 and the 50 is below the 200, so neither branch holds and the name is a range. This is the case the rule is shaped for: reading the close against one average alone would call it an uptrend, and reading the swings alone would call it a downtrend, since the last swing low is below the one before it.

properties.aRowForEveryMember: the row count equals the membership expectation's currentMembers, which is 4, and not the count of names carrying a tranche
properties.theDepartedGetNoRow: AAL and XRAY are constituents and not members tonight, so neither has a ladder row
properties.thePlanIsEmptyAndSaysWhy: at 4.1 every plan carries no tranche, no exit and no invalidation, and states that they are built from 4.4. A plan that is empty and states its reason is a different object from a plan that is absent
properties.noDownttrendInThisFixture: none of the four is in a downtrend, so the branch that produces no tranches at all is asserted over constructed input rather than over these bars
properties.noNotClassifiedInThisFixture: all four hold a full year, so all four have a 200-day average and two swings of each kind. The fourth state is asserted over constructed input for the same reason
properties.atMostThreeTranches: MSFT and NFLX each have more eligible bands than three and take the three nearest, which is section 17's count
properties.aStraddlingBandKeepsItsFullWidth: AAPL's first tranche runs 299.7415 to 320.28 with the close at 319.97 inside it, and the band is not trimmed to the close
properties.theStopIsTheBandBeneathAndNotTheTrancheB: AAPL's first tranche stops at 283.439, which is the average-only band beneath it and not the 273.5141 band that carries the second tranche
properties.theTrailingStopIsNeverLooserThanTheRange: every uptrend stop is the higher of the band beneath and the swing low beneath, so no stop in this fixture sits below the band the range rule would have given it
properties.theFractionsSumToTheWhole: each name's traded exits carry one over their count, so they sum to one over the position that exists rather than to a capital figure
properties.aSkippedExitIsListedRatherThanOmitted: MSFT and NFLX each carry a row for the exit they do not trade, with the reason on it

tranches.note: at most three per name, nearest first. The condition is the pattern the price has made at that band, tested in the stated order so exactly one applies, and ReachesTheZone is the absence of any of the four rather than a fifth pattern: a tranche where none has occurred is not actionable yet and says so.

invalidation.note: the lowest price the structure depends on, which is the lowest stop the tranches carry. AAPL and KEYS take theirs from the trailing rule, which is what gives their lowest tranche a stop at all: under the range rule alone the structure would end at that tranche's own low edge.

skipped.note: bands below the close with no anchor other than a moving average carry no tranche, and they are still stops: a band that cannot be bought is a level the price has to break. AAPL's 283.439 is its 200-day average and is the first tranche's stop while carrying no tranche of its own, which is the rule doing both things at once.

NFLX: 86.8835 is resistance and not a candidate

stops.note: the trend decides the stop. NFLX is the range and its three stops are the bands beneath, which is the range floor. The three uptrends take the higher of the band beneath and the most recent swing low beneath the tranche, so the stop rises as the structure makes higher lows and is never looser than the range rule.

whereTheTrailingRuleBites.KEYS: its first tranche's stop moves from the band at 288.5134 to the swing low at 293.55, which is the only tranche in this fixture where the trailing rule is tighter than the band beneath
whereTheTrailingRuleBites.AAPL and KEYS second tranches: each is the lowest support band its name has, so the range rule gives them no stop at all and the trailing rule gives them one: 264.5978 and 266.47
whereTheTrailingRuleBites.MSFT: every one of its three takes the band, because its swing lows beneath each tranche are further away than the band is. Its third tranche is the case that shows why the rule takes the higher of the two: the last swing low beneath 476.2534 is 376.6809, a hundred points down, and a trailing stop there would be looser protection than the range rule gives

exits.note: one per resistance band above the price, nearest first, at most five. An exit closer than two typical days' moves to the blended entry is listed and not traded, the blended entry being the mean of the first two tranche zones' midpoints. Each traded exit sells an equal fraction of what is held, and the highest traded one is a trailing rule rather than a price.

skipped.MSFT: its only resistance band sits 16.90 above the blended entry against a bar of 23.65, so every exit it has is listed and not traded and it has no top of the ladder at all. A plan that says take nothing here is a different object from one with a trailing rule attached to nothing.
